offense_focus: How does BAL's pass rate over expected and early-down pass/run mix shift by down and distance, and where would HOU's defense be most exposed?

How deep is BAL's average target depth and which targets absorb the largest share, and can HOU's secondary handle those downfield throws?

defense_focus: How does BAL's defense allow pass rate over expected and EPA on early downs, and where can HOU's offense exploit that by down and distance?
Does BAL's pressure proxy (sacks plus QB hits) and blitz rate suggest HOU's offensive line will face heavy pressure, and which pass rushers drive it?
How many players does BAL put in the box on runs, and does its run defense give up success or explosives to HOU's preferred run directions?
Where does BAL's defense rank in third-down stops and red zone defense, and which HOU offensive situations are most likely to succeed against it?
Do BAL's sacks and explosive plays allowed come against play action or screens, and how does that match HOU's play-action and screen rates?

Which HOU players are listed on the latest injury report, and how much of HOU's pass-rush, coverage, or run-game snap and target share is at risk for this game?
If BAL's top receiver or running back is limited or out, how does their target or rush share shift to other players, and what does that change in BAL's depth and explosive-play profile?
Are any BAL defensive linemen or edge rushers limited, and how would that change BAL's pressure proxy and blitz rate against HOU's offensive line?
If HOU's key offensive skill players or linemen are limited, which backups would absorb their snaps and targets, and how does that change HOU's pass rate and red zone efficiency against BAL?

defense_analyst.prose: Baltimore allows 0.05 EPA per pass play [dc1] over 386 dropbacks [dc2] and holds the run to -0.02 EPA per play [dc3], ranking 18th in overall EPA allowed [dc4]. Expect pressure: BAL sends five or more rushers on 33.2% of dropbacks [dc5] and averages 4.4 rushers [dc6], yet its pressure proxy (sacks plus QB hits) is 17.1% [dc7], so the blitz is a real threat but not an automatic sack factory. Against the run, BAL puts 6.5 defenders in the box [dc8] and allows explosives on 7.8% of runs [dc9] and 8.8% of passes [dc10]. HOU has been efficient throwing (0.14 EPA per pass [dc11]) but poor running (-0.10 EPA per run [dc12]), so the game plan should lean on the pass and avoid forcing the run into a stacked box. BAL is 10th in third-down stops, allowing conversions on 36.8% of attempts [dc13][dc14], but it is 20th in red zone TD rate allowed at 62.5% [dc15], though that rests on only 40 red zone drives [dc16] and is a small sample. sections.body: Baltimore's kicking changed hands mid-season. T. Loop made 13 [kc1] of 17 [kc2] field goals before R. Patterson took over and has gone 3 [kc3] of 3 [kc4] since. Overall Baltimore is 81.0% [kc5] on 21 [kc6] attempts, and 100.0% [kc7] on 6 [kc8] long tries, too small a sample to bank on late. Punts net 41.7 yards [kc9] on 47 [kc10] punts, so expect Houston to start deep after most of them. Kickoffs are touchbacks only 22.0% [kc11] of the time on 50 [kc12] kicks. Baltimore special-teams EPA is -0.07 per play [kc15] on 309 plays [kc16], versus 0.00 [kc17] for Houston on 282 plays [kc18].

sections.heading: Injuries and availability
sections.body: Baltimore's Outs are DT Nnamdi Madubuike (hamstring), who played 70.3% of snaps [ic2] across 8.0 games [ic3] earlier in the season, CB Marlon Humphrey (personal matter), who played 79.0% of snaps [ic5], and S Jaylinn Hawkins (knee). Expect more interior rotation and a thinner secondary. Houston's Outs are DE Danielle Hunter (hamstring), who played 75.6% of snaps [ic8] across 8.0 games [ic9], so edge pressure falls to backups. WR Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) has 3.3% of targets [ic11], RB Woody Marks (concussion) carries 45.7% of rushes [ic13], and TE Brevin Jordan (foot) has 0.6% of targets [ic15]. Questionable for Houston are G Wyatt Teller (back), LB Jacob Hummel (groin) and CB Jaylin Smith (hamstring).

sections.heading: Key matchups
sections.body: Third-and-long is the first fight. Baltimore throws on 80.2% of third downs [mc1] over 131 plays [mc2] yet converts only 38.9% [mc3], 16th [mc4]. With Hunter out after playing 75.6% of snaps [mc6] and Madubuike out after playing 70.3% of snaps [mc8], generate pressure with disguised interior blitzes and coverage that holds on third-and-long. Second, Henry runs at the edges: he takes 72.3% of carries [mc9], with designed runs left 41.9% [mc10] and right 43.7% [mc11] versus 14.4% [mc12] up the middle. Set the edges first, since Houston's own run game is at -0.1 EPA per run [mc13]. Third, attack the thinner secondary deep. With Humphrey out after playing 79.0% of snaps [mc15] and Hawkins out, Houston's passing offense at 0.14 EPA per pass [mc19] should target the back end early, with Flowers (25.4% of targets [mc20]) the primary target. Fourth, field position: Baltimore's punts net 41.7 yards [mc23] and land deep in Houston's territory on 40.4% [mc24] of punts, so Houston should expect to start deep after Baltimore punts.
